questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.

options.text: Louder than
Quieter than
About as loud as

questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is quieter than other vehicle horns. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it for safety.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not encouraged because you won't get used to one part of the lane.
Discouraged because it confuses other drivers.
Good if you are adjusting to changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good if you are adjusting to changing road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move your position in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If you carry a load on your motorcycle, it should be:

options.text: Carried over the rear axle.
Carried on the gas tank in front of you.
Piled against a sissy bar or frame on the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carried over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Loads should be over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may go over the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You can ignore no passing zone markings if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You must stay within the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must happen within the speed limit and only where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Keep a shorter distance from the vehicle ahead.
Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, increase your distance from other vehicles. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When carrying a load, it should be secured:

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low to protect your motorcycle's balance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and let traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if safe. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane away from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther away.
Is not recommended because it may cause the passing driver to move back into your lane too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the passing driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may signal the other driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.
Avoid talking and unnecessary movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking and unnecessary movement.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move unnecessarily while riding. They should get on after the engine starts and sit as far forward as comfortable.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean no passing. Dashed white lines mean passing is allowed if safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles travel slower than 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: Tell your passenger to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Mount the motorcycle after you start the engine.
Sit as far back on the motorcycle as possible.
Hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Keep their legs away from the muffler.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far back on the motorcycle as possible.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should mount after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chain, and other moving parts.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that increases their visibility.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce their reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, choose a lane position that makes you most visible. Cover the clutch and both brakes to reduce your reaction time. Slow down when approaching. Do not change your speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle responds to directional changes:

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. With this added weight, the motorcycle responds more slowly to your movements. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
Be able to keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start turning. Shifting gears during a turn can suddenly change the power to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly to avoid skidding.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when approaching an intersection. Cover the clutch and both brakes to reduce the time you need to react if needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a factor in determining a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: A person's blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on body weight, how much alcohol they drink, and how fast they drink it. It is always safest to not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors do. They also make objects appear farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: There is the greatest potential for conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic:

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles and other vehicles have the most conflicts. Ride carefully when approaching intersections.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should maintain a following distance of at least:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. When conditions are poor, use a larger distance.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: In bright daylight.
At dusk.
At night.

questions.correctAnswerText: In bright daylight.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during bright daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle steady.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can tip the bike over. Use only the rear brake to slow down during the turn.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. Intoxicated people cannot operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: You are passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic. Where should you ride?

options.text: In the left part of your lane.
In the right part of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic. This keeps you away from dangers like opening car doors and people stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.
